correctness.rationale: Upper R≤1+o(1) is direct, with the exceptional prime 2 handled. Six forms and their required local admissibility/complexity were independently checked; Green–Tao gives a positive quantitative count on fixed positive boxes. The checker passed its finite tests; the infinite claim relies on the cited unconditional theorem.

originality.rationale: The nearest 2026 paper establishes separate limit sets on C3 and joint curves on B3, not the full joint C3 rectangle; its Lemma 5 is acknowledged and reused. A previous same-map half-sum-prime subfamily has a strict inequality excluding (3/4,5/32), which the new construction attains in the joint limit. Broad primary and targeted indexed searches found no stronger covering statement. Unindexed equivalence and older inaccessible journal full text are recorded risks.
residual_risks: An unindexed identical squarefree joint classification could exist.
An older 2012 full journal article could contain an unobserved relevant result; only the abstract and later direct discussion were read.
The theorem follows from the published six-form lemma plus a new real parameter-surjectivity argument, so the advance is a complete classification, not a new prime-pattern theorem.

value.rationale: A natural complete joint-limit classification for the full squarefree three-prime family directly complements an important new paper proving only marginals there and a nonrectangular joint set on repeated-prime inputs. The previously known restricted subfamily omits explicit positive interior pairs; this result locates all such pairs and gives a uniform-in-X lower bound per fixed neighborhood. This resolves a substantive dependence question not answered by separate limits.
